title: Rates of Return for GIC and Temasek Holdings
what_it_is: Rates of Return for GIC and Temasek Holdings

sections.label: GIC return gap and comparisons
sections.summary: An MP asked why GIC's return gap versus its reference portfolio is higher over five years than 20 years, and how GIC and Temasek compare with other sovereign wealth funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Finance (a) why is the gap between GIC's nominal return and its reference portfolio return higher over the past five years versus the past 20 years; (b) how have GIC and Temasek Holdings performed in terms of annualised rate of return over the past 10 years versus major international sovereign wealth funds, such as those of Norway, Qatar, UAE, China, Hong Kong, Australia and Saudi Arabia; and (c) how do GIC and Temasek Holding's total management and operating expenses as a share of assets managed compare against the average for leading global sovereign wealth funds.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: But since Mr Perera has asked the question, let me quote the answer from page 15 of the GIC Annual Report, which states "…the difference in the returns between the GIC Portfolio and Reference Portfolio is largely due to the difference in risk exposures.

sections.label: Sovereign wealth fund comparisons
sections.summary: The reply states it is not meaningful to compare returns and expenses across entities globally because they have different mandates, risk profiles and operating constraints.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Mr Perera also asked for a comparison of GIC and Temasek with other Sovereign Wealth Funds, in terms of their returns and expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: It is not meaningful to compare returns and expenses across different entities globally as they have different mandates, risk profiles and operating constraints.

sections.label: Government evaluates long-term returns
sections.summary: The Government evaluates the entities' performance by long-term returns, considering risk exposure and market trends, and views GIC and Temasek as having performed creditably.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Instead, the Government evaluates the investment entities' performance by looking at their long-term returns, taking into account risk exposure, underlying market trends and other factors relevant to each entity.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: On the whole, the Government's view is that GIC and Temasek have performed creditably in challenging market conditions.

sections.label: Benchmarks used for GIC
sections.summary: The speaker says the Reference Portfolio is the primary benchmark, but other investors and benchmarks like MSCI are also tracked, with performance judged against risk taken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Just a quick clarification of what the Minister has said.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, is it right to say that the benchmarking is done only with respect to the Reference Portfolio which is the primary means of benchmarking good performance and differentiating good from bad performance right now with GIC?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Of course, we always look at other investors, not necessarily Sovereign Wealth investors, because GIC also engages external fund managers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, there is always a look at what other investment entities are achieving for the risks they are undertaking and the returns they are achieving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We can also track performance by looking at the benchmarks like MSCI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There is a range of benchmarks that we look at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But, ultimately, when we look at GIC's performance, we look at the risk that we have accorded to them, how much risk they are taking based on the budget that is allocated to them and the returns that are commensurate with the risk that they have taken.
